title: Participle clauses with adverbial meaning (1)
summary: Причастные обороты (-ing, having + V3, being + V3, not + -ing) вместо придаточных времени, причины и результата, и правило совпадения подлежащего.
ru:
## Что это такое
Причастный оборот с обстоятельственным значением — это «сжатое» придаточное предложение. Он убирает союз и подлежащее, оставляя только причастие, и работает как обстоятельство времени, причины или результата. Привычнее всего он звучит в письменной речи: в статьях, отчётах, прозе. В разговоре англичане скорее скажут *As I was tired, ...*, чем *Being tired, ...*.
> Realising she was late, Kate began to run. — Поняв, что опаздывает, Кейт побежала. (= *As she realised she was late...*)
Для вас это знакомая конструкция: английские обороты соответствуют русским деепричастным. **-ing** ≈ «читая», **having + V3** ≈ «прочитав», **Not -ing** ≈ «не зная».

## Четыре формы и их смысл
| Форма | Смысл | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| **V-ing** | одновременно с главным действием или сразу перед ним | Opening the drawer, he found a letter. |
| **Having + V3** | действие завершилось раньше главного | Having read the contract, she signed it. |
| **Being / Having been + V3** | то же, но в пассиве | Having been warned twice, he ignored the sign. |
| **V3** (без being) | пассив, «будучи сделанным» | Written in haste, the letter was full of errors. |

## -ing: одновременность, последовательность, результат
> Hearing the alarm, everyone ran outside. — Услышав сигнал, все выбежали. (две быстрые подряд идущие реакции)
> The factory closed down, **leaving** two hundred people jobless. — Фабрика закрылась, оставив двести человек без работы. (-ing в конце = следствие)
Если нужно подчеркнуть, что первое действие *полностью закончено* и разделено по времени со вторым, берите **having + V3**: *Having worked abroad for years, she found her home town strange.* Сравните: *Walking home, I met Ben* (по дороге) и *Having walked home, I felt exhausted* (дошёл — и уже устал).

## Причина: особенно с состояниями
Глаголы состояния (be, know, feel, have, live) в таком обороте почти всегда передают **причину**.
> Not knowing the way, we asked a passer-by. — Не зная дороги, мы спросили прохожего.
> Being a doctor, she stays calm in emergencies. — Будучи врачом, она сохраняет спокойствие.
> Feeling unwell, Tom stayed at home.
*Being* часто опускают: *Tired after the flight, he went straight to bed.*

## Пассив и отрицание
Пассивное причастие — частая конструкция в описаниях: *Built in 1890, the bridge is still in use.* Но **being built** = «строящийся сейчас», а **having been built** = «будучи уже построенным»: *Having been built on sand, the house began to sink.*
Отрицание ставится **перед** причастием: *Not having received a reply, I wrote again.* Вариант *Having not received* встречается, но в аккуратном письме предпочитают первый.

## Главная ловушка: подлежащее должно совпадать
Тот, кто выполняет действие в обороте, должен быть подлежащим главного предложения.
- ~~Walking down the street, the rain started.~~ → Walking down the street, **I felt** the rain start. / **As I was walking** down the street, the rain started.
- ~~Having finished the report, the computer was switched off.~~ → Having finished the report, **she switched off** the computer.
Это называют *dangling participle* («висячее причастие»). В русском тот же запрет — на «деепричастие без подлежащего». Исключения — устойчивые обороты: *Judging by..., Generally speaking, Considering her age, Strictly speaking*.
en:
## What it is
A participle clause with adverbial meaning is a shortened adverbial clause. It drops the conjunction and the subject and keeps only the participle, which gives the reason, the time or the result of the main action. It is typical of written English; in speech people usually prefer *As I was tired, ...* to *Being tired, ...*.
> Realising she was late, Kate began to run. (= As she realised she was late...)

## Four forms
- **V-ing**: happens at the same time as the main action, or just before it. *Opening the drawer, he found a letter.*
- **Having + past participle**: finished before the main action. *Having read the contract, she signed it.*
- **Being / Having been + past participle**: the passive. *Having been warned twice, he ignored the sign.*
- **Past participle alone**: a passive without *being*. *Written in haste, the letter was full of errors.*

## -ing: time, sequence, result
> Hearing the alarm, everyone ran outside. (quick reaction)
> The factory closed down, **leaving** two hundred people jobless. (the -ing clause after the main clause shows the result)
Use **having + past participle** when the first action is clearly complete and earlier: *Having worked abroad for years, she found her home town strange.* Compare *Walking home, I met Ben* (on the way) and *Having walked home, I felt exhausted* (I arrived, then felt tired).

## Reason, especially with state verbs
With be, know, feel, have, live the clause usually gives a **reason**.
> Not knowing the way, we asked a passer-by.
> Being a doctor, she stays calm in emergencies.
*Being* is often dropped: *Tired after the flight, he went straight to bed.*

## Passive and negative
*Built in 1890, the bridge is still in use.* Note: **being built** = in the process of being built; **having been built** = already built: *Having been built on sand, the house began to sink.*
**Not** goes before the participle: *Not having received a reply, I wrote again.* *Having not received* exists but sounds less careful.

## The main trap: the subject must match
The person or thing doing the action in the participle clause must be the subject of the main clause.
- ~~Walking down the street, the rain started.~~ → Walking down the street, **I felt** the rain start.
- ~~Having finished the report, the computer was switched off.~~ → Having finished the report, **she switched off** the computer.
This is called a *dangling participle*. Fixed expressions are an exception: *Judging by..., Generally speaking, Considering her age, Strictly speaking*.
structure:
## Формы
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| V-ing | одновременность / быстрая последовательность / результат | Seeing the queue, he left. |
| Having + V3 | действие раньше главного | Having eaten, we went out. |
| Being + V3 / V3 | пассив, причина или описание | (Being) delayed by fog, the flight was cancelled. |
| Having been + V3 | пассив, завершено раньше | Having been told the truth, she resigned. |
| Not + форма | отрицание | Not wanting to be late, we took a taxi. |

## Формулы
> Придаточное: **As / When / After + S + V** → Оборот: **V-ing / Having + V3**, + главное предложение
> As she didn't know the way, she asked. → **Not knowing** the way, she asked.

> Результат: Главное предложение, + **V-ing**
> The storm hit the coast, **destroying** hundreds of homes.

## Подлежащее
| Правильно | Неправильно |
|---|---|
| Opening the door, **he** smelled gas. | ~~Opening the door, gas was smelled.~~ |
| Written in haste, **the letter** had errors. | ~~Written in haste, I found errors in it.~~ (подлежащее не письмо) |

exercises.title: Причастие по смыслу
exercises.instruction: Вставьте причастие от глагола в подсказке в нужной форме (с not или having, если нужно).

items.text: {{Having read}} the contract twice, Dana signed it.
{{Not knowing}} the local language, Tom relied on a phrasebook.
{{Opening}} the envelope, she found a cheque inside.
{{Having been injured}} in the first half, the striker could not play on.
The film, {{shot}} entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
{{Not having been invited|Having not been invited}} to the meeting, he stayed at his desk.
{{Having lived}} abroad for a decade, Nina found her home town strange.

exercises.example: Because she was tired, she went to bed. → **Being tired**, she went to bed.

exercises.title: Сожмите придаточное
exercises.instruction: Дополните предложение причастным оборотом, равным придаточному в первой части.

items.text: After she had checked the schedule, Lena booked a flight. → {{Having checked}} the schedule, Lena booked a flight.
Because it was designed by an amateur, the website was hard to use. → {{Designed|Being designed|Having been designed}} by an amateur, the website was hard to use.
As he realised he had lost the keys, Paul turned back. → {{Realising|Realizing|Having realised|Having realized}} he had lost the keys, Paul turned back.
The company cut costs and so lost its best engineers. → The company cut costs, {{losing}} its best engineers.
Since I don't have a car, I take the bus. → {{Not having}} a car, I take the bus.
When he saw the police, the thief ran off. → {{Seeing|On seeing|Upon seeing|Having seen}} the police, the thief ran off.

items.q: ___ in 1887, the tower has become a symbol of the city.
items.why: Башню построили — нужен пассив **Built**. *Being built* значило бы «строится сейчас».

items.q: ___ by the noise, the baby started to cry.
The factory closed down, ___ hundreds of workers jobless.
items.why: Результат в конце предложения передаётся формой **-ing**: leaving.

items.q: ___ ill for weeks, he finally went to a doctor.
items.why: Болезнь длилась до момента визита, то есть закончилась раньше: **Having been**.

options: a dolphin suddenly jumped out of the water
we saw a dolphin jump out of the water
the water seemed full of dolphins
items.why: Идти мог только человек: подлежащее главной части — **we**. Остальные варианты — «висячее причастие».

options: Having arrived late, the meeting had already begun.
Having arrived late, we found the meeting had already begun.
Arrived late, the meeting had already begun.
items.why: Подлежащее оборота и главной части должно совпадать: приехали **we**.

options: Not having understood the question, the answer was wrong.
Not having understood the question, she gave a wrong answer.
Not understood the question, she gave a wrong answer.
items.why: Не поняла вопрос **she**, а не «ответ»; форма — Not having understood.

options: Delayed by fog, the flight was eventually cancelled.
Delayed by fog, the cancellation was announced at noon.
Delaying by fog, the flight was eventually cancelled.
items.why: Задержан был рейс: пассив **Delayed** и подлежащее *the flight*.

options: Having seen by the guard, the thief ran away.
Having seen the guard, the thief ran away.
Having being seen the guard, the thief ran away.
items.why: Вор сам увидел охранника — активная форма **Having seen**.

options: Taking the key out of his pocket, the door was opened.
Taking the key out of his pocket, he opened the door.
Take the key out of his pocket, he opened the door.
items.why: Ключ достаёт человек, а не дверь: **he** в главной части.

items.q: The report, ___ in a hurry, contained several errors.

exercises.title: Перепишите с причастным оборотом
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, начав его так, как указано в конце.

items.prompt: As she had no experience, she didn't apply for the job. Начните: Having no
answers: Having no experience, she didn't apply for the job.
Having no experience, she did not apply for the job.

items.prompt: After he had cleaned the kitchen, Sam made dinner. Начните: Having
answers: Having cleaned the kitchen, Sam made dinner.

items.prompt: Because I was exhausted, I fell asleep on the sofa. Начните: Exhausted
answers: Exhausted, I fell asleep on the sofa.
Being exhausted, I fell asleep on the sofa.

items.prompt: The storm hit the coast and destroyed hundreds of homes. Используйте: destroying
answers: The storm hit the coast, destroying hundreds of homes.

items.prompt: As we didn't want to be late, we took a taxi. Начните: Not
answers: Not wanting to be late, we took a taxi.

items.prompt: The villa, which was built in 1920, is now a museum. Используйте: Built
answers: Built in 1920, the villa is now a museum.
The villa, built in 1920, is now a museum.

exercises.title: Переведите на английский
exercises.instruction: Переведите, используя причастный оборот. Ключевые слова даны.

items.prompt: Не зная, что делать, она позвонила начальнику. (know / call / boss)
answers: Not knowing what to do, she called her boss.
Not knowing what to do, she called the boss.

items.prompt: Прочитав письмо, он позвонил юристу. (have read / lawyer)
answers: Having read the letter, he called the lawyer.
Having read the letter, he called a lawyer.
Having read the letter, he called his lawyer.

items.prompt: Родившись в Бишкеке, она хорошо знает горы. (be born / know)
answers: Having been born in Bishkek, she knows the mountains well.
Born in Bishkek, she knows the mountains well.
Being born in Bishkek, she knows the mountains well.

items.prompt: Не получив ответа, мы написали ещё раз. (receive / write)
answers: Not having received a reply, we wrote again.
Not having received an answer, we wrote again.
Not having received a response, we wrote again.
Not having received a reply, we wrote once more.
Not having received an answer, we wrote once more.

items.prompt: Здание, построенное в 1950 году, скоро снесут. (build / pull down)
answers: Built in 1950, the building will soon be pulled down.
The building, built in 1950, will soon be pulled down.
Built in 1950, the building will soon be demolished.
The building, built in 1950, will soon be demolished.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Закончите предложения причастным оборотом. Образцы — для самопроверки.

items.sample: Having finished work today, I went for a long walk.

items.prompt: Not knowing what to cook, I ...
items.sample: Not knowing what to cook, I ordered a pizza.

items.prompt: Tired after a long week, I ...
items.sample: Tired after a long week, I stayed in bed until noon.

items.prompt: Напишите предложение о городе, где вы живёте, с оборотом Built / Founded ...
items.sample: Founded in the eleventh century, the town has kept much of its old charm.

items.prompt: Напишите, что вы сделали вчера, с оборотом ..., leaving / making / causing ...
items.sample: I missed the bus, making me late for the first lesson.
